status: hardware timestamp approach selected for feasibility comparison; no RF clock precision measurement yet

bluetooth_reference.finding: Connected peripherals track their piconet central clock. A scatternet contains independent piconets, with bridges maintaining separate offsets and multiplexing time; it does not create one automatic global clock. A piconet supports at most seven active peripherals.
bluetooth_reference.sdk_check: Pinned ESP32 Kconfig supports1..7 BR/EDR ACL connections, default2. The prior two-link configuration was not a hardware two-link maximum.
bluetooth_reference.decision: Retain BTstack for phone A2DP/BLE. Do not add a mandatory Bluetooth clock link to every broadcast listener; it consumes connection/radio resources and does not directly discipline the I2S sample clock.

wifi_references.finding: esp_wifi_get_tsf_time reads the TSF clock. Unconnected station mode returns zero until associated and receiving a beacon. Reading the API alone cannot provide a shared clock to unassociated raw listeners.

Espressif identifies RX timestamps as the internal MAC clock and recommends associated STA/AP TSF for shared timing. The discussion distinguishes TSF from RX MAC time and notes callback scheduling delay. Its direct-register example is ESP32-S3-specific and must not be copied onto original ESP32.
Pinned internal MAC clock getter is32-bit microseconds, wraps after about71.6min, and documents sleep-related precision conditions. Use the pinned API in task context; ISR safety is not established.

candidate_router_free_clock_path: Investigate source native Wi-Fi beacon TSF stamping as the broadcast reference, rather than putting an enqueue-time timestamp into an arbitrary data frame.
At each listener capture source beacon timestamp and local hardware MAC RX timestamp before deferred processing. Filter exact admitted source/BSSID and bind a generation.
Measure the timestamp point and fixed PHY/frame offset; do not assume RX timestamp equals beacon TSF or the local esp_timer clock.
Estimate phase and frequency relationship between source clock and local MAC clock using successive captures, with loss/outlier limits and explicit uncertainty.
Schedule each logical SBC group at one source presentation timestamp. Source and followers use that same timeline, regardless of which copy succeeds.
Discipline the independent I2S output rate or resample decoded PCM with bounded correction. Clock timestamps alone do not frequency-lock the DAC.
Investigate beacon-only operation with unassociated listeners to avoid a per-listener Wi-Fi association requirement; verify actual hardware stamping and Bluetooth coexistence before adopting it.
associated_ap_reference: Compare with both boards associated to a common AP and using TSF as a reference; an ESP32 SoftAP is not a100-associated-client solution.
material_limits: Raw/sniffer reception with Bluetooth is documented unstable; hardware timestamps do not fix RF absence.
1us timestamp units are resolution, not proven synchronization accuracy.
No automatic clock-domain equivalence between TSF, MAC RX timestamps, esp_timer and I2S DMA/sample counters.
Driver restarts and source handovers must explicitly reset/rebind clock generations.
100-150ms is end-to-end latency, not a clock accuracy specification.
implemented_foundation: wmp_time.c extends32-bit MAC captures across wrap and derives absolute sample presentation times without accumulating group rounding. Affine estimator, hardware capture integration and DAC servo remain to be implemented.
host_tests: build/protocol-1793555261329793600/receipt.json:15 pass, including wrap, stale capture and absolute sample timing; no RF/audio qualification
